news.title: FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites
news.description: The U.S. Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s plan to place a constellation of data centers in orbit. The authorization, valid for 15 years, allows the deployment of up to one million satellites.

news.title: OpenAI tests private inference for businesses
news.description: OpenAI’s Private Inference runs a company’s queries on its best models without OpenAI being able to see the data. The service is being tested with early business customers.

news.title: Neuralink gets FDA approval to test its implant for ALS
news.description: Neuralink has received FDA authorization to launch the pivotal LINK study, which will evaluate its brain implant in people severely disabled by ALS. U.S. adults with the disease can sign up for the patient registry.

news.title: Character.AI reportedly wants to sell millions of user conversations
news.description: Character.AI is reportedly considering selling millions of its users’ conversations to the highest bidder.

news.title: OpenAI fixes a ChatGPT billing error
news.description: OpenAI fixed a billing error affecting ChatGPT and promises to make it 40% worse.

news.title: OpenAI tests protection for business prompts during processing
news.description: OpenAI is testing a method designed to protect businesses’ prompts while its models process them.

news.title: Epochal launches Time Portal, an “AI time machine”
news.description: Startup Epochal, founded by former xAI members, unveiled Time Portal, an environment that confines AI agents to the Internet as it existed on a given date over the past 30 years. The agents then use this historical data to make forecasts, with sometimes surprisingly robust results.

news.title: Claude supports skills, tasks, and interactions via MCP
news.description: Anthropic is launching Skills over MCP in public beta for Claude, allowing Model Context Protocol servers to publish workflows and instructions with their tools. The Tasks and Elicitation features are also available for long-running and interactive work, while file uploads will roll out soon.

news.title: SpaceX prepares to deploy computing capabilities in orbit
news.description: The U.S. space industry is described as generally unhealthy, while SpaceX is particularly well positioned to install computing infrastructure in orbit. The company has been investing in this direction for more than a decade, while other tech giants lack ideas for future growth.

news.title: OpenAI claims to have demonstrated that the matrix multiplication exponent is 9/4
news.description: OpenAI claims to have proved that ω, the matrix multiplication exponent, is exactly equal to 9/4.

news.title: Anthropic’s IPO tests confidence in AI spending
news.description: Anthropic’s IPO represented a new test for bets on AI-related spending.

news.title: OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic are designing their own chips
news.description: OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic are using AI to design their own chips.

news.title: Elon Musk and SpaceX promise one share for every active Trump account
news.description: Elon Musk and SpaceX promise one share for every active Trump account.

news.title: OpenAI warns some heavy ChatGPT users about advanced limits
news.description: A small share of heavy ChatGPT users could reach limits more quickly when Chat and Work share the same usage counter. The rollout is expected to expand in December.

news.title: Meta reportedly negotiating with Amazon to let its Muse agent make purchases
news.description: Amazon and Meta are reportedly negotiating an agreement that would allow Meta’s Muse agent to make purchases on Amazon. The placement of ads and display of search results remain to be decided.

news.title: New York bans AI chatbot-equipped toys for five years
news.description: New York has become the second state, after California, to ban toys equipped with AI chatbots. The five-year ban will take effect 90 days after it is signed.

news.title: PrismML reduces a 27-billion-parameter coding model to 5.9 GB
news.description: Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B reduces a 27-billion-parameter programming model to 5.9 GB, about nine times smaller than usual. The open-source model can run on a Mac or an iPhone.

news.title: Carry saves and searches conversations from multiple AI assistants
news.description: Carry saves ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok conversations as Markdown files in a chosen folder, then lets users search them.

news.title: ChatGPT merges Chat and Work spaces with a shared quota
news.description: OpenAI is rolling out a single interface combining Chat and Work to some Pro subscribers, with a shared usage counter. A broader rollout is planned for December and could cause heavy users to hit their limits more quickly.

news.title: AI safety advocates turn away from Anthropic
news.description: According to The Information, some AI safety advocates are leaving Anthropic, believing that its rapid progress is increasing risks. They particularly criticize the company’s acceleration since its IPO.

news.title: Nvidia suspends AI server deliveries to four Asian countries
news.description: Nvidia has asked its manufacturing partners to suspend AI server deliveries to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. The decision follows a new U.S. rule requiring licenses to export advanced chips to these countries.

news.title: WhatsApp now lets users schedule messages
news.description: WhatsApp is adding a feature that lets users schedule the automatic sending of a text, photo, or video from 10 minutes to 14 days in advance. Messages remain end-to-end encrypted, and the feature will roll out worldwide over the coming weeks.

news.title: 1Password suffers intrusion into its backend systems
news.description: Hackers accessed 1Password’s backend systems after compromising an employee’s GitHub account and deploying malicious code. According to the company, customer vaults, passwords, and recovery keys were not affected, but some administrative data was stolen.

news.title: Dario Amodei rejects the idea of handing human free will to AI
news.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called the idea that he wants humans to surrender their free will to AI “absurd.” He said society must never sacrifice its legitimacy or self-determination in the name of efficiency or security.

news.title: X adds parental controls for the first time
news.description: X is adding its first parental controls.

news.title: Apple removes MiniMax chatbot from the App Store over safety concerns
news.description: Apple removed the MiniMax AI chatbot from the App Store because of concerns related to child safety.

news.title: Complaint reveals alleged pressure from Trump on Intel
news.description: A lawsuit reveals the pressure Donald Trump allegedly exerted on Intel.

news.title: Claude rewrote the API that powers it, but verification proved more difficult
news.description: Claude rewrote the API that powers the Claude service. Verifying its work proved more difficult.

news.title: Chinese company says robots will soon handle household chores
news.description: A Chinese electric vehicle company says robots could perform household chores within one to two years.

news.title: The New York Times bans Photoshop 2027 for its AI tools
news.description: The New York Times is banning the use of Adobe Photoshop 2027 because of its AI tools and metadata disclosure requirements.

news.title: Kagi launches a Gmail competitor
news.description: Kagi, presented as an alternative to Google’s search engine, is launching a competing service to Gmail.

news.title: U.S. officials reportedly considered reinstating Jensen Huang at Nvidia
news.description: U.S. defense officials reportedly considered using a Cold War-era law to force Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO after his resignation, according to a report.

news.title: Nvidia sellers seek new buyers amid U.S. restrictions
news.description: Sellers of Nvidia chips are seeking new buyers as the United States limits China’s access to AI chips, according to sources cited by CNBC.

news.title: My terrifying journey to becoming a real estate agent
news.description: It is far too easy to obtain a real estate agent’s license, which should concern American buyers. The author recounts discovering the seedy side of every real estate sale.

news.title: Separate server and model costs to reduce an agent’s bill
news.description: Hosting a coding agent in the cloud creates two separate bills: infrastructure costs, charged for the entire runtime, and model costs, tied to calls and tokens used. To avoid paying for idle time, shut down workspaces after tasks and track the two types of costs separately.

news.title: Nothing introduces Ear (note), earbuds that take notes with AI
news.description: Ear (note) records calls through the earbuds and in-person conversations through microphones built into the charging case. An app then turns the recordings into transcripts and quick summaries.

news.title: Grok Bot can call businesses and compile their responses
news.description: Grok Bot can be configured to call suppliers, restaurants, repair shops, or service providers, ask a series of questions, and compile the answers into a comparison. The user must approve each call, then can save the process as a skill and daily routine.

news.title: Grok Bot can monitor prices before Black Friday
news.description: Grok Bot can monitor prices on Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and other sites every few hours, then alert the user when the best deals appear.

news.title: Claude Fable 5.2 users are already exploring ambitious applications
news.description: Anthropic published an initial look at real-world uses of Claude Fable 5.2 less than two weeks after its launch. Some examples go far beyond the most obvious use cases.

news.title: Independent developer creates a game with AI’s help in six days
news.description: A solo game developer says they used AI for the code and part of the visual work on their first game. Six days after launch, the title had surpassed a sales level rarely reached by independent developers.

news.title: Google files a patent to put you in personalized movies and TV shows
news.description: Google reportedly filed a patent for an AI-powered television network capable of using a person’s photos and voice to insert them into personalized movies and TV shows.

news.title: Rackspace shuts down Spot after security breach
news.description: Rackspace will permanently shut down its Spot Kubernetes service on December 8 at 5 p.m. Central Time. Customers must migrate their workloads and download their data, while API tokens, kubeconfigs, and Kubernetes secrets are considered potentially compromised.

news.title: HPE shares fall as AI-related margin decline weighs
news.description: HPE shares fell about 16%, as margin guidance overshadowed an improved forecast for 2027 revenue growth. Demand for AI servers is supporting revenue, but component costs are rising faster than selling prices.

news.title: European IT spending expected to jump 9.9% in 2027
news.description: Gartner forecasts that European IT spending will reach $1.57 trillion in 2027, a 9.9% increase. Demand for AI infrastructure and rising server prices are driving the growth, while software purchases are shifting toward systems that coordinate multiple business functions.

news.title: Why legacy systems are becoming increasingly risky
news.description: The reliability of aging infrastructure depends in part on maintenance, vendor support, replacement parts, monitoring, and redundancy. Software becomes riskier as workloads evolve and patches and support end, making timely upgrades or retirement necessary.

news.title: An AI agent reveals a technical team’s informal rules
news.description: Matthew Finlayson describes building an agent to route customer issues to engineering teams. The project uncovered undocumented responsibility rules and improved routing accuracy from about 60% to 95%.

news.title: Datadog launches Bits Maintenance to automate infrastructure fixes
news.description: Datadog introduces Bits Maintenance, an AI teammate designed to automate fixes and upgrades for open-source software. Available in preview, the tool tracks versions and vulnerabilities, analyzes changes, prepares upgrade plans, and executes pull requests under user-defined guardrails.

news.title: Workday’s CIO prepares IT for the AI era
news.description: Rani Johnson explains how Workday is rebuilding its data lake, identity infrastructure, and Salesforce environment to strengthen its AI foundations. Collaboration with training helped increase enterprise AI adoption from under 50% to more than 96% by addressing skills and behavior challenges.

news.title: Microsoft modernizes retail kiosks with Autopilot and Intune
news.description: Microsoft describes moving its checkout devices from domain-joined and Configuration Manager-managed systems to Windows Autopilot and Intune. The new setup uses Windows 11 Enterprise LTSC, Microsoft Entra join, provisioning without individual user accounts, and certificates for Wi-Fi access.

news.title: Capital One reduces human rework with its multi-agent system
news.description: Capital One reduced the rate of human rework on AI-generated customer-support summaries by about 80% using its MACAW agent system.

news.title: Germany’s federal IT provider chooses OpenProject as a Jira alternative
news.description: ITZBund, the central IT provider for Germany’s federal administration, has chosen OpenProject as an open-source alternative to Jira.

news.title: Google reorganizes the “More actions” panel for Meet rooms
news.description: Menus on Google Meet room controllers will prioritize the most frequently used commands. Early access rollout will begin on December 2, followed by broader rollout on December 11.

news.title: AI models surpass theoretical physicists on many technical tasks
news.description: Publicly available AI models crossed a threshold in August and now outperform most theoretical physicists on many technical tasks. They can perform complex analytical calculations, produce lengthy proofs, and turn well-defined problems into code with minimal instruction.

news.title: Software engineering enters an advanced automation phase
news.description: A growing share of software work can be automated opaquely by agent teams, swarms, or factories when the target is sufficiently verifiable. Advances in agents’ problem selection, intent, and taste require continuously redefining what needs human intervention.

news.title: Engineers who use AI can improve software quality
news.description: Equating engineers who use AI with executives who weaken their companies is harmful. With real responsibility and good models, engineers can build the safeguards, proofs, and fixes they previously lacked time to create.

news.title: Anthropic operates like an infrastructure provider specializing in frontier AI
news.description: Anthropic is committing tens of billions of dollars in computing capacity to selling an advantage in AI and performance. The company is portrayed as a heavily indebted utility provider with an R&D department, able to preserve its margins through growing demand for frontier intelligence.

news.title: A guide to getting started in angel investing
news.description: Angel investing can potentially multiply a small investment many times over, and it is possible to start with $5,000. This article explains where beginners can find founders, how to select them, and how much to invest.

news.title: CSS mixins enable code blocks to be reused
news.description: A CSS mixin is a named block of code that developers can define once and reuse elsewhere in a stylesheet.

news.title: Ladybird’s first downloadable alpha is promising
news.description: Ladybird’s rendering engine and LibJS JavaScript engine were written entirely from scratch. Its first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable.

news.title: An introduction to open-source chip design
news.description: This article introduces readers accustomed to a more software-focused view of computing to the open-source chip design toolchain.

news.title: The Jevons paradox may no longer explain rising usage
news.description: Cheaper tokens increase usage within the same step, but moving to the next step is an organizational rather than pricing problem.

news.title: Bicameral Labs seeks to create non-conscious neural networks
news.description: The founder of Bicameral Labs believes it is possible to create neural networks while ensuring they are not conscious, or by minimizing the risk that they become conscious.

news.title: Cloud coding agents generate two distinct costs to budget for
news.description: A cloud-hosted coding agent incurs separate infrastructure costs, tied to machine usage time, and model costs, tied to tokens consumed. To limit spending, shut down workspaces when they are idle and track the two costs in separate columns.

news.title: A millennial popularizes Friendsgiving in a retirement community
news.description: A millennial introduced Friendsgiving to her neighbors in a retirement community, who first had to understand why the event was held on a different day. Four years later, it is the building’s most anticipated event.

news.title: AI May Have Contributed to Recent Outages, But Not as Expected
news.description: AI likely played a role in the recent outages, but not in the way expected.

news.title: Cloudflare and Vercel Call for Calm Amid AI-Related Fears
news.description: As social media imagined that AI could paralyze civilization, leaders at Cloudflare and Vercel called for calm.

news.title: JPMorgan Supplier Breach Shows AI-Amplified Risks
news.description: A breach at a JPMorgan supplier illustrates why AI could make old vulnerabilities easier to exploit.

news.title: Black October PHP Vulnerability Illustrates AI Risks
news.description: The Black October PHP vulnerability shows why AI could make exploiting old flaws easier.

news.title: Experts Fear a “Tsunami of Vulnerabilities” With AI
news.description: Some experts believe AI could trigger a “tsunami of vulnerabilities.”

news.title: Jensen Huang’s Return Divides Investors and Tech Leaders
news.description: Jensen Huang’s return divided investors and technology industry leaders.

news.title: AI Is Creating Founders Too Important to Disappear
news.description: Jensen Huang’s return renewed the question of whether AI is creating founders who have become too important to fail.

news.title: Jensen Huang Says Nvidia Doesn’t Need a Plan B
news.description: Jensen Huang said Nvidia did not need a plan B.

news.title: S&P Global Warns of Nvidia’s Dependence on Jensen Huang
news.description: S&P Global’s warning makes the question of Jensen Huang’s succession at Nvidia harder to ignore.

news.title: Michael Burry Criticizes Nvidia’s Dependence on Its Leader
news.description: Michael Burry’s criticism adds to questions about Nvidia’s dependence on Jensen Huang.

news.title: Market Decline Raises Questions About the Profitability of AI Spending
news.description: The market decline reflects growing doubts about whether companies investing heavily in data centers can generate sufficient returns.

news.title: Anthropic Reveals Nearly $895 Billion in Commitments
news.description: The amended filing submitted by Anthropic reports nearly $895 billion in commitments.

news.title: Anthropic Shares Fall Below Their IPO Price
news.description: Anthropic shares fell below their IPO price less than a week after going public, suggesting investors still doubt that revenue will exceed costs.

news.title: Google and Amazon Could Sell Their Chips to Other Customers
news.description: Google and Amazon could sell their chips to other customers.

news.title: Data Center Opposition Could Limit Cloud Capacity
news.description: Opposition to data centers could make it harder for major cloud providers to compete with existing capacity.

news.title: Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade Postponed Until Saturday
news.description: A storm postponed Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade until Saturday for the first time in its history, disrupting the plans of more than 3.5 million regular spectators.

news.title: Weather Delays More Than 6,500 U.S. Flights
news.description: On Wednesday, weather delayed more than 6,500 flights in the United States and canceled about 160.

news.title: Nine Things to Know About the Historic Super El Niño
news.description: The article presents nine things to know about this year’s historic Super El Niño.

news.title: Terence Tao Calls for a Transition to “Math 2.0”
news.description: Terence Tao is calling for a transition to “math 2.0” following AI’s spectacular advances.

news.title: Anthropic Gets More AI With Less Computing Power
news.description: Anthropic is getting more AI with less computing power, which benefits the company but hurts other players.

news.title: Teen Entrepreneur Generates Six Figures in Revenue in One Month
news.description: A young entrepreneur ignored the advice to follow his passion. His business generated six figures in revenue in a single month.

news.title: The 10 Best Movies and Shows to Watch This Weekend
news.description: The article recommends the 10 best movies and shows to watch over Thanksgiving weekend.

news.title: Bill Ackman Shares Carl Icahn’s Declining Fortune
news.description: Bill Ackman cannot resist sharing information about Carl Icahn’s declining fortune.

news.title: Consumers Are Abandoning Gift Cards for More Personal Gifts
news.description: Gift cards are losing ground as consumers put more effort into their gifts this year.

news.title: Google Is Building a Tollbooth for AI Agents
news.description: Google is building a new tollbooth for AI agents, which could encourage Microsoft to do the same.

news.title: New Notices Exclude Borrowers From a Student Repayment Plan
news.description: Student loan borrowers are receiving new notices informing them that they have been excluded from an income-driven repayment plan.

news.title: Family Who Came to See the Thanksgiving Parade Won’t Be Able to Attend
news.description: Someone brought their family to New York for the Thanksgiving Parade, an event that had been on their dream list since childhood. They ultimately will not be able to see it.

news.title: Claude turns the United States into a Civilization map
news.description: Andrej Karpathy asked Claude Opus 5.5 to turn the United States into a Civilization map using public data. After seven hours and 45,000 lines of code, the map combines 31 sources on a hexagonal grid.

news.title: Anthropic’s CEO rejects the idea of an AI-governed society
news.description: Dario Amodei believes humans should not hand society’s major decisions over to AI. He advocates governing AI through legitimate democratic processes, while distinguishing task execution from writing collective rules.

news.title: A coding agent must demonstrate every performance gain
news.description: The Agentic Algorithm Engineering project requires Claude Code and Codex to define a benchmark, a metric, correctness checks and a budget before any optimization. In examples involving KaHIP and VieCut, the agent kept only changes that were faster and correct.

news.title: Perplexity launches a spoiler-free Internet
news.description: Perplexity has created a spoiler-free Internet to test whether an AI can predict an election without Google revealing the result to it.

news.title: Democratic senators call for new AI restrictions
news.description: Several Democratic senators have called for new AI restrictions following reports that laboratory employees fear some internal models are too dangerous to release.

news.title: Agents already control some of the computing used by Gemini
news.description: Koray Kavukcuoglu, a vice president at Google DeepMind, said that AI agents now control some of the computing used in Gemini experiments, while estimating that full self-improvement remains a long way off.

news.title: Cloudflare adds search for AI agents
news.description: Cloudflare’s Search for Agents adds a search endpoint to a website that AI agents can query and that returns Markdown. The feature has been available in beta from the dashboard.

news.title: CodeRabbit Verify tests applications and posts errors on PRs
news.description: CodeRabbit Verify runs an application in a sandbox on demand, then posts encountered issues to the pull request along with recordings, screenshots and logs. The service is in public beta.

news.title: MemoryWorks centralizes engineering decisions and team knowledge
news.description: MemoryWorks brings an engineering team’s decisions and knowledge together in a searchable knowledge base for employees and AI agents, with links to the sources.

news.title: Claude writes 80% of Anthropic’s code, but Amodei wants to limit its autonomy
news.description: According to Anthropic, Claude wrote more than 80% of the code merged into its codebase in June 2026. Dario Amodei wants to set a limit on recursive self-improvement and refuses to let AI build future models alone without human oversight.

news.title: Google imagines a personalized AI TV channel where you would play the lead role
news.description: A patent describes “My Channel,” a service that continuously produces AI-generated videos from personal data, with the option to appear as the protagonist. The system would also incorporate personalized ads.

news.title: The Hera probe reveals a stadium-sized crater on Dimorphos
news.description: The European Hera probe photographed the damage from DART’s deliberate impact on the asteroid Dimorphos. The crater spans its entire width, and hundreds of rocks now orbit the asteroid.

news.title: Google DeepMind entrusts Gemini experiments to AI agents
news.description: AI agents independently launch and run some of the experiments preparing future Gemini models. DeepMind leaves their internal reasoning untrained so humans can review it.

news.title: MIT improves climate forecasts using extreme scenarios
news.description: By training its models on deliberately abrupt changes in CO2 and methane, an MIT team has produced more robust climate emulators. A single training run is now sufficient instead of six to eight.

news.title: Researchers define five trust conditions for AI agents
news.description: Ai2 surveyed 17 scientists about using AI agents in their work. They identified five conditions for trust: validation, privacy, objectivity, accountability and transparency.

news.title: Embo-Harness lets AI models directly control robots
news.description: This framework allows multimodal models to plan actions and use tools to control robots from a simple instruction. It achieves an 83.3% success rate on RoboLab-120 and succeeds in 15 of 20 trials on real robots.

news.title: Vibe coding pushes synthesizer makers toward open source
news.description: Hobbyists are modifying electronic instrument firmware with agents such as Claude and the Reverse Engineer Anything tool. InMusic, the parent company of Akai, Moog and Native Instruments, has chosen to open-source its devices’ code.

news.title: NVIDIA releases training data for Nemotron 3.5 Parse
news.description: NVIDIA has open-sourced the training data for Nemotron 3.5 Parse, including 9.98 million charts, one million tables and 7.9 million multilingual pages. The model converts page images into structured data.

news.title: Chinese labs estimate they are up to nine months behind the United States
news.description: Chip restrictions, limited access to Nvidia hardware and anti-distillation measures are weighing on DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and Alibaba. DeepSeek researchers reportedly estimate internally that they are no more than nine months behind.

news.title: Nvidia risks a ratings downgrade amid political controversy
news.description: S&P placed Nvidia on negative watch following controversy involving Jensen Huang and an alleged investigation by the Department of Justice. The agency could downgrade the company from AA to AA- within 90 days.

news.title: CIA and U.S. Intelligence Agencies Hit by Intrusion
news.description: The CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence discovered an intrusion into a public intelligence analysis system. The data was not classified, but the extent of the breach remains unknown.

news.title: SoftBank rebounds after a 14.8% stock-market plunge
news.description: After falling 14.8% in a single session, SoftBank rebounded more than 11% on Thursday. Asian chip stocks also rose after doubts about the profitability of AI spending.

news.title: Access to new medicines in Switzerland: an emerging risk?
news.description: The editorial questions whether people in Switzerland may soon lose access to new medicines, despite having the ability to develop or produce them.

news.title: Parkinson’s: sleep brain waves linked to hallucinations
news.description: A study seeks to explain why some people with Parkinson’s experience hallucinations or cognitive difficulties by linking these symptoms to sleep-related brain waves.

news.title: Nuclear fusion: EPFL solves a more-than-40-year-old mystery
news.description: Since 1982, physicists have known that plasma heated beyond a certain threshold can suddenly change its behavior. EPFL has provided an answer to this mystery involving nuclear fusion plasma.

news.title: Proteins from ancient viruses control our genes
news.description: A significant portion of the human genome comes from ancient mobile genetic elements, some of which originated from ancient viruses. These proteins now control the activity of our genes.

news.title: Cryptography: the quantum threat could become critical as early as 2030
news.description: Quantum computers cannot yet break major encryption systems. However, the threat could become critical as early as 2030.

news.title: Riemann Hypothesis: an AI and a mathematician propose two proofs
news.description: One of mathematics’ greatest open problems may have reached a historic milestone. An AI and a mathematician claim to have produced two competing proofs.

news.title: In Basel, AI reveals how the DNA environment activates genes
news.description: Nearly all cells possess the same DNA, but they do not activate the same genes. Researchers in Basel are using AI to study the role of the DNA environment.

news.title: DNA repair: how the cell chooses its strategy
news.description: When both strands of a chromosome break, the cell must act quickly to prevent damage. Swiss researchers reveal how it chooses its repair strategy.

news.title: Tuberculosis: a shared membrane strengthens bacterial resistance
news.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis can form long, membrane-like structures. This shared membrane helps the bacteria resist the body’s defenses.

news.title: Primordial plasma challenges an Einstein diffusion model
news.description: More than 120 years after Albert Einstein’s work on Brownian motion, a study challenges a diffusion model applied to primordial plasma.
